headline: 7 critical reports. Rescues under way in Bowness and Bragg Creek; High River and Siksika Nation are evacuating.
worst_areas: High River — whole neighbourhoods under water
Bowness, Calgary — boat rescues in progress
Bragg Creek — people reported on rooftops
roads_and_bridges: Highway 1 closed west of Bragg Creek
Highway 2 closed at High River until further notice
Deerfoot Trail closure reported, not yet confirmed
evacuations: Siksika Nation — reception centre at the Enmax Centre in Calgary
Canmore — town-wide evacuation order in effect
Tsuut'ina Nation — residents near the river leaving within the hour
Mission, Calgary — families still waiting for transport
summary: Water is still rising along the Bow and Highwood rivers. The most urgent reports are people stranded in homes in Bowness and on rooftops near Bragg Creek. High River is the worst-hit town in this set. Three First Nations are reporting damage or evacuation: Siksika, Stoney Nakoda and Tsuut'ina, with Siksika the largest at roughly 1,000 members moving to the Enmax Centre. Road access into the southwest is cut in several places, so aid coming from Edmonton and Okotoks should expect detours. Two claims about official status — a Deerfoot Trail closure and the Okotoks shelter being full — have not been confirmed against a source.
